title: Capture-recapture histories of 285 Cabanis's greenbuls in the Ngangao forest fragment, Taita Hills, Kenya, 1996-2000 and 2005-2009
creator: Husemann, Martin; Cousseau, Laurence; Callens, Tom; Matthysen, Erik; Vangestel, Carl; Hallmann, Caspar; Lens, Luc
citation: Husemann, M., Cousseau, L., Callens, T., Matthysen, E., Vangestel, C., Hallmann, C., & Lens, L. (2015). Data from: Post-fragmentation population structure in a cooperative breeding Afrotropical cloud forest bird: emergence of a source-sink population network [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.8n5d7
abstract: Mist-net capture-recapture histories of Cabanis's greenbul (Phyllastrephus cabanisi) in the Ngangao cloud-forest fragment of the Taita Hills, Kenya, over two sampling periods (1996-2000 and 2005-2009) with irregular sessions; birds of the two periods are not linked.
samplingProtocol: Repeated mist-netting sessions in the forest fragment; birds individually colour-ringed; one capture record per bird per session.
geographicCoverage: Ngangao fragment, Taita Hills, Taita-Taveta County, Kenya; no coordinates deposited

notShipped.genetics: microsatellite genotypes and nestling / fledgling records (not survey data)

notes: Periods number the sessions through P1 then P2; session start dates are as deposited (often the 15th of the month, so approximate) and are in __periods, not a date column. Each bird's rows run from its first capture to the last session of its sampling period.
